*Sasol Board Didn't Declare Final Dividend as Net Debt Remained Above Targeted Threshold
Sasol Net Profit Surges on Cost Cuts, Higher Energy Prices
Sasol reported a sharp increase in net profit for fiscal 2026, as the company moved to rein in costs and benefited from higher energy prices toward the end of the year.

The South African chemicals-and-energy group said Tuesday that it made a net profit of 12.15 billion South African rand ($753.9 million) for the year ended June 30, up from 6.77 billion rand a year before.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization were 17% higher at 60.705 billion rand. The company attributed the performance to a combination of actions to lower costs and a more supportive environment during the final quarter of the year that led to higher sales volumes and increases in crude oil prices and refining margins.
Full-year turnover was 272.12 billion rand, up 9%.
Sasol said it reduced its net debt by 11% to end the year at $3.3 billion, but its board decided against declaring a final dividend since debt remained above its $3 billion target.
